note: ONE registry — every tooltip, tap sheet, legend row and EDITH explanation reads this file. Plain English only.

cash_on_hand.name: Cash on hand
cash_on_hand.meaning: The money sitting in the business bank accounts right now.
cash_on_hand.computed: The closing balances of the three CommBank accounts (everyday, saver, and the tax account), read from Xero.
cash_on_hand.default_from: Xero's bank feeds — they can run up to a day behind the bank.

committed_mrr.name: Committed monthly revenue
committed_mrr.meaning: The recurring revenue clients are signed up to pay each month — money coming IN, never a cost.
committed_mrr.computed: Adds up every active client's monthly amount from the finance sheet, including renewals that are recorded there.
committed_mrr.default_from: the finance workbook's client list, refreshed every couple of hours.

ar_outstanding.name: Money owed to us
ar_outstanding.meaning: What clients were expected to have paid by now but haven't. For your eyes — the system never chases anyone.
ar_outstanding.computed: What each client's plan says they should have paid so far, minus what has actually landed in Stripe.
ar_outstanding.default_from: the finance workbook's payment plans matched against real Stripe payments.

cash_net_mtd.name: Cash gained or lost this month
cash_net_mtd.meaning: How much the bank balance has actually moved since the 1st of the month.
cash_net_mtd.computed: Today's bank balance minus the balance at the start of the month.

operating_net_mtd.name: Operating profit this month
operating_net_mtd.meaning: Money collected this month minus normal running costs — tax money is shown next to it, never mixed in.
operating_net_mtd.computed: Stripe payments received this month, minus this month's running costs (wages, tools, ads). Tax set-asides sit beside the number.
operating_net_mtd.default_from: Stripe payments and the cost categories in Xero.

ltv_cac.name: Lifetime value vs cost to win a client
ltv_cac.meaning: For every dollar spent winning a client, how many dollars they pay us over their whole contract.
ltv_cac.computed: The average full contract value of new clients, divided by the full cost of winning one (ads plus commissions plus sales tools).
ltv_cac.default_from: this month's signed clients and ad spend.
ltv_cac.good: 3-to-1 is a common healthy benchmark, not a target.

ltgp_cac.name: Lifetime profit vs cost to win a client
ltgp_cac.meaning: Like the tile beside it, but counts only the PROFIT in each contract after delivery costs.
ltgp_cac.computed: Contract value times the profit margin, divided by the cost of winning the client.
ltgp_cac.default_from: this month's signed clients; the margin uses last year's 42.9% until this year's books settle.
ltgp_cac.good: 3-to-1 is a common healthy benchmark, not a target.

cohort_cash_roas.name: Cash back on this month's ads
cohort_cash_roas.meaning: Of the money spent on ads this month, how much cash the clients those ads produced have paid so far.
cohort_cash_roas.computed: Cash collected from this month's new clients, divided by this month's ad spend. It starts low and climbs as instalments land.
cohort_cash_roas.default_from: Stripe payments from this month's signed clients and the Meta ads bill.

pulse_show_rate.name: Show rate
pulse_show_rate.meaning: Of the sales calls booked recently, how many people actually turned up.
pulse_show_rate.computed: Calls attended divided by calls booked, over the last 30 days.
pulse_show_rate.default_from: the lead tracker; the small count is shown next to it — a handful of calls makes this jumpy.

pulse_close_rate.name: Close rate
pulse_close_rate.meaning: Of the people who turned up to a call recently, how many signed.
pulse_close_rate.computed: New clients divided by attended calls, over the last 30 days.
pulse_close_rate.default_from: the lead tracker and the signed-deal list; small counts make it jumpy.

pulse_booked_calls.name: Booked calls, next 7 days
pulse_booked_calls.meaning: How many sales calls are on the calendar for the coming week.
pulse_booked_calls.computed: Counts upcoming appointments in the booking system; cancelled ones never count.
pulse_booked_calls.default_from: the GHL calendar — read-only, nothing is ever changed there.

exec_verdict.name: The verdict line
exec_verdict.meaning: One sentence on whether this month's ad spend is working, decided by the numbers underneath.
exec_verdict.computed: Compares signed contract value and collected cash against the month's ad spend, and says when the cash catches up.

card_sales.name: Ads & sales
card_sales.meaning: Everything about the ad-to-client pipeline: the funnel, the sales team, sources, and this month's closes.

card_receivables.name: Receivables
card_receivables.meaning: Who owes what, and how overdue it is. Your visibility only — nobody gets chased automatically.

card_renewals.name: Renewals & churn
card_renewals.meaning: Which clients are coming up to the end of their term, who renewed, and who's at risk.

card_projection.name: Forward projection
card_projection.meaning: Where monthly revenue goes from here: what's locked in, what's still undecided, and the terms ending soon.

card_outflows.name: Outflows & BAS
card_outflows.meaning: Where the money goes each month — running costs in one lane, tax and personal in their own lanes.

card_unit_econ.name: Unit economics
card_unit_econ.meaning: The cost of winning a client versus what they're worth, in detail.

card_cash.name: Cash & capital
card_cash.meaning: Bank position, runway, and where spare cash could work harder.

card_team.name: Team & strategy
card_team.meaning: Team cost, hiring headroom, and the biggest growth constraints.

card_brief.name: Morning brief
card_brief.meaning: The long-form daily read: summary, actions, and verdicts.

card_scale.name: Scaling compass
card_scale.meaning: Plan 2027: type a spend or a target and see leads, calls, clients, cash and hires.

card_decisions.name: Needs your ruling
card_decisions.meaning: Items only you can decide — each with its evidence.

card_csm.name: Client success
card_csm.meaning: The client-success cockpit (only you can see this card).

card_worklog.name: Work log
card_worklog.meaning: What the system and the team changed, when.

card_bookkeeping.name: Bookkeeping queue
card_bookkeeping.meaning: Money entries waiting for Piolo to fix at the source.

card_system.name: System health
card_system.meaning: Whether the data feeding every number is fresh and the pages are rendering cleanly.

section-brief.name: Morning brief
section-brief.meaning: The 60-second daily read: cash, revenue, clients and the two value-for-money ratios.

section-exec.name: Executive summary
section-exec.meaning: A few sentences on the state of the business, written from the live numbers.

section-actions.name: Action items
section-actions.meaning: Things the numbers say need doing, ranked.

section-kpis.name: Key numbers strip
section-kpis.meaning: The headline numbers side by side: revenue, cash collected, margin, active clients.

section-capital.name: Capital allocation
section-capital.meaning: Whether spare cash is sitting idle and where it could work harder.

section-cash-position.name: Cash position
section-cash-position.meaning: Bank balances, Stripe money on its way, tax set aside, and how many months the cash lasts.

section-stripe-health.name: Stripe health
section-stripe-health.meaning: Payments, failures and refunds over the last 30 days.

section-forward.name: Forward projection
section-forward.meaning: Monthly revenue projected ahead: the locked-in part never moves with the slider; the undecided part does.

section-trend.name: Revenue trend
section-trend.meaning: Monthly recurring revenue over the past year.

section-revenue.name: Revenue views
section-revenue.meaning: The same money seen two ways: what landed in the bank vs what the books recognise. Never added together.

section-churn.name: Churn risk
section-churn.meaning: Clients whose term is ending and what's declared about them; the sheet stays Piolo's to edit.

section-month-perf.name: Month performance
section-month-perf.meaning: This month vs last: leads, calls, clients, cash.

section-waterfall.name: Profit waterfall
section-waterfall.meaning: From revenue down to profit, step by step, with tax shown in its own lane.

section-outflow.name: Outflow truth
section-outflow.meaning: Each month's money-out split into running costs, tax, and personal — never blended.

section-commissions.name: Commission tracker
section-commissions.meaning: What the setters and closer are owed this month, per deal.

section-metrics.name: Unit economics panel
section-metrics.meaning: Revenue, profit, cost per client and payback, from the books.

section-perf-analysis.name: Performance analysis
section-perf-analysis.meaning: The funnel across different time windows.

section-speed-to-lead.name: Speed to lead
section-speed-to-lead.meaning: How fast new leads get their first call — slow kills conversion.

section-funnel.name: Sales funnel
section-funnel.meaning: Leads to calls to shows to clients, as a funnel.

section-health.name: Client health
section-health.meaning: Every active client and how their account is doing.

section-verdicts.name: Verdicts
section-verdicts.meaning: Plain-language calls the system is confident about, with the leaks it sees.

section-team.name: Team & hiring power
section-team.meaning: Current team cost and what a new hire would do to the numbers.

section-deficiency.name: Growth constraints
section-deficiency.meaning: What's most holding growth back, ranked by impact.

section-pipeline.name: Sales pipeline
section-pipeline.meaning: Deals by stage in the CRM, read-only.

section-dq-loss.name: Lost-deal intelligence
section-dq-loss.meaning: Why deals didn't close, grouped by reason.

section-offers.name: Offer mix
section-offers.meaning: Which packages new clients are buying.

section-lead-roi.name: Lead source ROI
section-lead-roi.meaning: What each lead source costs per signed client.

section-reps.name: Rep performance
section-reps.meaning: Setters and closers side by side: volume, conversion, trend.

section-cohort.name: Client retention grid
section-cohort.meaning: How long clients from each signing month stayed.

section-reconciliation.name: Client reconciliation
section-reconciliation.meaning: Where two systems disagree about a client — flagged, never silently merged.

section-quality.name: Data quality
section-quality.meaning: Which data sources are healthy and which are limping.

section-action-feed.name: What needs action
section-action-feed.meaning: Everything needing a decision, in one ranked feed.

section-bas.name: BAS & tax set-aside
section-bas.meaning: The tax bill building up this quarter and the money set aside for it.

section-forecast-cash.name: Cash runway forecast
section-forecast-cash.meaning: Where the bank balance is heading over the next 13 weeks.

section-forecast-mrr.name: Revenue forecast
section-forecast-mrr.meaning: Where monthly revenue is heading under best, base and worst cases.

section-ratio-tiles.name: Value-for-money ratios
section-ratio-tiles.meaning: Lifetime value and profit vs the cost of winning a client, by window.

section-decision-cards.name: Needs your ruling
section-decision-cards.meaning: Decisions waiting for you, each with its evidence.

section-ar.name: Receivables detail
section-ar.meaning: Expected vs received per client, with how overdue each is.

section-roas.name: Three ways to read ad returns
section-roas.meaning: Cash-back, contract-value and lifetime views of the same ad spend — labelled, never blended.

section-csm-card.name: Client success card
section-csm-card.meaning: Shortcut to the client-success cockpit (owner only).

section-ops-cards.name: Work log & bookkeeping
section-ops-cards.meaning: Shortcuts to the work log and the bookkeeping queue.

section-adlink.name: Ad tracking link
section-adlink.meaning: The creative scoreboard lives on its own page.

section-expiring.name: Terms ending soon
section-expiring.meaning: Clients whose contract ends in the window — declare what's real, or flip the what-if switch to see the effect.

section-burn-accurate.name: Burn & runway
section-burn-accurate.meaning: What it costs to run the business each month (tax excluded and shown beside), and how long the cash lasts.

section-render-health.name: Page health
section-render-health.meaning: Whether the dashboard itself is rendering cleanly in people's browsers.

burn_opex.name: Monthly running cost
burn_opex.meaning: What it costs to run the business for a month — wages, tools, delivery — with tax and ad spend counted elsewhere.
burn_opex.computed: The average of recent months' running costs from the books, minus ads and commissions (they're shown in their own places).
burn_opex.default_from: the last few months of Xero, categorised by account.

burn_tax.name: Tax set aside
burn_tax.meaning: Money reserved for the tax bill — kept beside the running costs, never hidden inside them.
burn_tax.computed: The set-aside the BAS estimate says to hold.

burn_net.name: Net burn
burn_net.meaning: Running costs minus the recurring revenue that's locked in — negative means the client base covers the costs.
burn_net.computed: Monthly running cost minus committed monthly revenue.

burn_runway.name: Runway
burn_runway.meaning: How many months the cash lasts if nothing changes.
burn_runway.computed: Cash in the bank (minus the tax set-aside) divided by the net burn.

exp_toggle.name: 'Resigns same deal' switch
exp_toggle.meaning: A what-if switch: see the future as if this client renews on the same deal. It changes the picture on screen only.
exp_toggle.changing: The chart and totals update as if they renew — but NOTHING is recorded. Use Declare… to record a real renewal.

exp_chip_actual.name: 'Declared' tag
exp_chip_actual.meaning: This client's renewal or extension has been properly recorded — it counts for real.

exp_chip_scenario.name: 'What-if' tag
exp_chip_scenario.meaning: You've flipped the switch on this client — the picture assumes they renew, but nothing is recorded.

exp_chip_slider.name: 'Slider rate' tag
exp_chip_slider.meaning: No decision on this client yet — the picture applies the renewal percentage from the slider.

exp_window.name: Window buttons (30/60/90)
exp_window.meaning: How far ahead to look for contracts ending.
exp_window.changing: Shows clients whose terms end within that many days.

exp_effective.name: The tally line
exp_effective.meaning: How many terms are ending, how many renewals are recorded, how many are what-ifs, and what rate applies to the rest.

sim_spend.name: Monthly ad spend
sim_spend.meaning: How much goes into ads each month in this what-if.
sim_spend.changing: Leads update from it (spend divided by cost per lead) — and everything downstream follows.
sim_spend.default_from: measured from your last 90 days of ads and the lead tracker.

sim_cpl.name: Cost per lead
sim_cpl.meaning: What one lead costs from ads.
sim_cpl.computed: Ad spend divided by the number of leads it produced.
sim_cpl.changing: With CPL unlocked, typing a new value recomputes whichever of spend/leads is not locked.
sim_cpl.default_from: measured from your last 90 days of ads and the lead tracker.

sim_leads.name: Leads per month
sim_leads.meaning: How many new enquiries a month of that spend buys.
sim_leads.computed: Ad spend divided by cost per lead.
sim_leads.changing: Typing a leads number works backwards to the spend needed at the current cost per lead.
sim_leads.default_from: measured from your last 90 days of ads and the lead tracker.

sim_lock.name: Lock
sim_lock.meaning: Pins one of the three numbers so edits move the other two around it.
sim_lock.changing: The locked field never changes; the other two answer your edits.

sim_cpl_mode.name: 'CPL rises as spend grows' switch
sim_cpl_mode.meaning: Off (normal): cost per lead stays fixed so you can see the straight spend-to-leads relationship. On: it climbs as spend grows, the way ad platforms really behave.
sim_cpl_mode.changing: On, big spend numbers buy fewer leads per dollar — the curve bends and the field shows the effective cost per lead at that spend.
sim_cpl_mode.default_from: the climb rate is an assumption you can change (the account's own history was too noisy to trust).

sim_sentence.name: The one-line result
sim_sentence.meaning: The three numbers in one sentence, always current.

sim_chart.name: Leads vs spend chart
sim_chart.meaning: The straight (or bending) line from spend to leads, with your current point marked.

chain_calls.name: How many calls does that book?
chain_calls.meaning: Leads times the booking rate — how many turn into a booked sales call.
chain_calls.computed: Leads × the rate at which leads book calls.
chain_calls.default_from: measured from your last 90 days of ads and the lead tracker; the count it's based on is written beside it.

chain_shows.name: How many turn up?
chain_shows.meaning: Booked calls times the turn-up rate.
chain_shows.computed: Calls × the rate at which booked people actually attend.
chain_shows.default_from: measured from your last 90 days of ads and the lead tracker.

chain_clients.name: How many sign?
chain_clients.meaning: People who turned up times the close rate — new clients per month.
chain_clients.computed: Shows × the close rate. Your 35% belief goes here if you want it.
chain_clients.default_from: measured from your last 90 days of ads and the lead tracker.

chain_cash.name: What do they pay us?
chain_cash.meaning: The cash those new clients pay — this month's deposits now, the rest over their contract — plus the monthly revenue they add.
chain_cash.computed: New clients × the package mix × what each package pays up front and over its term.
chain_cash.default_from: real deposits and contract values from recent signed clients.

chain_cost.name: What does it cost us?
chain_cost.meaning: The full cost of winning those clients, and the value-for-money ratios.
chain_cost.computed: Ad spend + sales commissions + sales tools, divided by the new clients — then contract profit divided by that cost.
chain_cost.default_from: commissions use last year's actual 6.3% of sales.

show_math.name: Show the math
show_math.meaning: Prints the arithmetic behind every step with the actual numbers, so you can check any line by hand.
show_math.changing: Turns the worked arithmetic on or off. What it prints is exactly what the page computed.

i_want.name: I want…
i_want.meaning: Type the result you want — leads, calls, clients, cash or added revenue — and it works backwards to the spend required.
i_want.computed: Runs the same chain in reverse at the current rates.
i_want.changing: Also shows what has to be true at every step, and what a better close rate would save.

ctl_spend_start.name: Monthly ad spend (plan)
ctl_spend_start.meaning: The spend the longer-range plan starts from.
ctl_spend_start.changing: Every planned month scales from it.
ctl_spend_start.default_from: measured from your last 90 days of ads and the lead tracker, unless marked as an assumption.

ctl_spend_shape.name: Spend shape
ctl_spend_shape.meaning: Whether planned spend stays flat or ramps monthly.
ctl_spend_shape.changing: Flat holds it; ramp grows it by the percentage each month.
ctl_spend_shape.default_from: measured from your last 90 days of ads and the lead tracker, unless marked as an assumption.

ctl_ramp_pct.name: Ramp % per month
ctl_ramp_pct.meaning: How fast planned spend grows, if ramping.
ctl_ramp_pct.changing: Higher grows spend—and every downstream number—faster.
ctl_ramp_pct.default_from: measured from your last 90 days of ads and the lead tracker, unless marked as an assumption.

ctl_cpl0.name: Cost per lead (plan)
ctl_cpl0.meaning: The cost per lead the plan assumes at today's spend.
ctl_cpl0.changing: Cheaper leads mean more leads for the same money.
ctl_cpl0.default_from: measured from your last 90 days of ads and the lead tracker, unless marked as an assumption.

ctl_epsilon.name: How fast CPL climbs
ctl_epsilon.meaning: How quickly leads get more expensive as spend grows. 0 = never; higher = faster.
ctl_epsilon.changing: Raise it and big spend plans buy fewer leads per dollar.
ctl_epsilon.default_from: measured from your last 90 days of ads and the lead tracker, unless marked as an assumption.

ctl_set_rate.name: Booking rate
ctl_set_rate.meaning: The share of leads that book a call.
ctl_set_rate.changing: More bookings per lead moves every later number up.
ctl_set_rate.default_from: measured from your last 90 days of ads and the lead tracker, unless marked as an assumption.

ctl_show_rate.name: Turn-up rate
ctl_show_rate.meaning: The share of booked calls where the person attends.
ctl_show_rate.changing: Fewer no-shows means more chances to close.
ctl_show_rate.default_from: measured from your last 90 days of ads and the lead tracker, unless marked as an assumption.

ctl_close_rate.name: Close rate (plan)
ctl_close_rate.meaning: The share of attended calls that sign.
ctl_close_rate.changing: Your strongest lever — small changes move everything.
ctl_close_rate.default_from: measured from your last 90 days of ads and the lead tracker, unless marked as an assumption.

ctl_renewal_rate.name: Renewal rate
ctl_renewal_rate.meaning: The share of clients who continue after their term ends.
ctl_renewal_rate.changing: Higher keeps the client base from shrinking as terms end.
ctl_renewal_rate.default_from: measured from your last 90 days of ads and the lead tracker, unless marked as an assumption.

ctl_commission.name: Commission share
ctl_commission.meaning: The slice of new-client cash paid as sales commissions.
ctl_commission.changing: Raising it increases the cost of each new client.
ctl_commission.default_from: measured from your last 90 days of ads and the lead tracker, unless marked as an assumption.

ctl_opex.name: Running costs per month
ctl_opex.meaning: Monthly cost of running the business — tax, ads and commissions all counted elsewhere.
ctl_opex.changing: Higher costs shorten runway and deepen any cash dip.
ctl_opex.default_from: measured from your last 90 days of ads and the lead tracker, unless marked as an assumption.

ctl_buffer.name: Minimum cash buffer
ctl_buffer.meaning: The bank balance the plan must never dip below.
ctl_buffer.changing: The plan flags CASH as the blocker in any month below it.
ctl_buffer.default_from: measured from your last 90 days of ads and the lead tracker, unless marked as an assumption.

ctl_hire_lead.name: Hiring lead time
ctl_hire_lead.meaning: Weeks between deciding to hire and the person starting.
ctl_hire_lead.changing: Longer lead time means hire warnings appear earlier.
ctl_hire_lead.default_from: measured from your last 90 days of ads and the lead tracker, unless marked as an assumption.

ctl_deal_mix.name: Deal mix
ctl_deal_mix.meaning: The share of new clients on each package.
ctl_deal_mix.changing: Shifting mix changes what an average new client pays.
ctl_deal_mix.default_from: measured from your last 90 days of ads and the lead tracker, unless marked as an assumption.

ctl_lag_curve.name: Time from lead to signing
ctl_lag_curve.meaning: How a month's leads spread their signings over that month and the next two.
ctl_lag_curve.changing: Measured from recent deals; it shifts when cash arrives.
ctl_lag_curve.default_from: measured from your last 90 days of ads and the lead tracker, unless marked as an assumption.

ctl_lanes.name: Markets (AU / US)
ctl_lanes.changing: US leads currently borrow the AU rates — the ad bill can't be split by country yet.
ctl_lanes.default_from: measured from your last 90 days of ads and the lead tracker, unless marked as an assumption.

accuracy_sentence.name: How accurate is this?
accuracy_sentence.meaning: One sentence on how close this model's predictions were to what actually happened over the last three months.
accuracy_sentence.computed: The model is re-run on each past month's real spend and compared with what really happened at every step.

confidence_word.name: Confidence word
confidence_word.meaning: 'Solid', 'fair' or 'rough' next to a rate — how much data sits behind it. Rough means treat it as a guess.
confidence_word.computed: Solid needs a good-sized count; rough means only a handful of examples.

presets.name: Presets
presets.meaning: One-click starting points: today's run-rate, +50% spend, or the saved Base 2027.
presets.changing: Loads those numbers into the simulator — nothing is saved until you save it.

solver.name: Target solver
solver.meaning: Type a revenue or cash target and a month; it finds the spend path that gets there, or says what breaks first.
solver.changing: Type a different target or month and it re-finds the spend path — or tells you what breaks first.

roadmap.name: The month-by-month plan
roadmap.meaning: Every month to Dec 2027: spend, leads, calls, clients, cash, costs, bank position — and the one thing holding that month back.

money_view.name: Money view
money_view.meaning: Cost per client (with and without commissions), payback time, and whether early payments cover the cost of winning clients.

team_view.name: Team view
team_view.meaning: How loaded each role is month by month, and when to hire.

hire_card.name: Hire card
hire_card.meaning: A dated instruction: hire this role by this month so they're productive when the workload arrives.
hire_card.computed: When a role's workload passes 100%, the card counts back the hiring lead time.

ranges.name: Show ranges
ranges.meaning: Shows a realistic band around the forecast instead of a single line — wide bands mean thin data.
ranges.changing: Runs the plan many times with the rates wobbled by how well-measured they are.

scenarios.name: Scenarios
scenarios.meaning: Save a set of inputs under a name, and compare saved sets side by side.
scenarios.changing: Saving stores the current inputs under the name; comparing runs each saved set and shows the end results side by side.

commit_plan.name: Commit as Plan 2027
commit_plan.meaning: Freezes a scenario as the plan of record so the dashboard can track actuals against it. It is a plan — never the actual books.
commit_plan.changing: Creates a new version of the plan; the pacing table starts comparing every month against it.

pacing.name: Plan vs actual
pacing.meaning: Each month's plan next to what really happened, with a hint at why they differ.

calibration.name: Calibration table
calibration.meaning: Predicted vs actual for each of the last three months, step by step.

capital_dip.name: Capital dip
capital_dip.meaning: The lowest the bank balance goes across the whole plan — the cash you must be able to survive.
capital_dip.computed: The minimum of the projected month-end bank positions.

binding_constraint.name: The blocker
binding_constraint.meaning: The one thing holding growth back that month: lead volume, sales capacity, delivery capacity, cash, or client losses — always named with the number that caused it.

level_simple.name: Simple view
level_simple.meaning: The three questions: what does spend buy, what does it turn into, what do you want. Nothing else.

level_advanced.name: Advanced
level_advanced.meaning: The detailed levers: cash timing, deal mix, commissions, capacity, ranges, market lanes.

level_plan.name: Plan
level_plan.meaning: Saved scenarios, the month-by-month roadmap, committing Plan 2027, and plan-vs-actual tracking.

drawer_cash_on_hand.name: Cash on hand — the working
drawer_cash_on_hand.meaning: The per-account bank balances behind the tile and when they were read.

drawer_committed_mrr.name: Committed revenue — the working
drawer_committed_mrr.meaning: Every client's monthly amount, where each came from, and the cross-checks.

drawer_meta_spend_mtd.name: Ad spend — the working
drawer_meta_spend_mtd.meaning: The Meta spend behind the number, day by day.

drawer_cash_collected.name: Cash collected — the working
drawer_cash_collected.meaning: Stripe's bank-truth payments beside the team-logged tracker cells — two different things, labelled.

drawer_ar_outstanding.name: Money owed — the working
drawer_ar_outstanding.meaning: Per client: what was expected, what arrived, and how overdue.

drawer_forecast_net.name: Forecast net — the working
drawer_forecast_net.meaning: The projection's assumptions and the three real month figures it must track.

drawer_three_nets.name: The three nets — the working
drawer_three_nets.meaning: Bank movement, operating profit, and expected month-end — three different questions, never blended.

drawer_burn_ex_tax.name: Burn — the working
drawer_burn_ex_tax.meaning: How the monthly running cost is built and why tax and ads sit outside it.

drawer_booked_calls.name: Booked calls — the roster
drawer_booked_calls.meaning: Every upcoming consult in the next 7 days with its time.

drawer_ltv_cac.name: Lifetime value ratio — the working
drawer_ltv_cac.meaning: The inputs behind the ratio: contract values, costs, and the renewal figure with how much data backs it.

drawer_ltgp_cac.name: Lifetime profit ratio — the working
drawer_ltgp_cac.meaning: Same as the value ratio but after delivery costs; the margin source is stated.
